claim_verbatim: It is unstoppable - renewables will make very little difference. By any objective measure, renewable energy is making very little headway
probability_words: will make very little difference / unstoppable
resolution_criterion: YES if global CO2 emissions path through 2035 shows renewables failed to bend emissions enough to stop warming acceleration (emissions still rising or flat high); NO if emissions fall materially on a renewables-led path.
resolution_rule_fixed: YES if global CO2 emissions path through 2035 shows renewables failed to bend emissions enough to stop warming acceleration (emissions still rising or flat high); NO if emissions fall materially on a renewables-led path.

claim_verbatim: Global heat into 2027 — High. The WMO outlook supports continued warmth as El Niño’s influence carries beyond its expected late-2026 peak.
context: Almanac watchlist item 1; High confidence on continued warmth into 2027.
source: Essay: The 1/1000 Year El Niño Almanac: 2026–2027 Chokepoints
resolution_criterion: YES if 2027 global mean surface temperature remains elevated near-record or record-class per major datasets; NO if 2027 is clearly cool relative to 2023–26.
resolution_rule_fixed: YES if 2027 global mean surface temperature remains elevated near-record or record-class per major datasets; NO if 2027 is clearly cool relative to 2023–26.
resolution_source_planned: NASA GISTEMP / Copernicus / NOAA global temp
notes: He notes WMO gives no probability 2027 alone sets a record. Qualitative High→0.80.

claim_verbatim: Andrew Watkins told ABC that 2027 is “almost a dead cert” to be the hottest year.
context: Craig relays BoM climatologist without contradiction in Almanac.
source: Essay: The 1/1000 Year El Niño Almanac: 2026–2027 Chokepoints
resolution_criterion: YES if 2027 is hottest year in instrumental record on at least two of NASA/Copernicus/NOAA; NO otherwise.
resolution_rule_fixed: YES if 2027 is hottest year in instrumental record on at least two of NASA/Copernicus/NOAA; NO otherwise.
consensus_source: BoM climatologist Andrew Watkins via ABC, as quoted
notes: Relayed third-party certainty he platformed. Confirm with Craig whether to count as his.

claim_verbatim: WMO puts persistence through February 2027 near 100%.
context: El Niño persistence cited in Almanac.
source: Essay: The 1/1000 Year El Niño Almanac: 2026–2027 Chokepoints
resolution_criterion: YES if El Niño conditions (NOAA CPC) persist through February 2027; NO if ENSO returns to neutral/La Niña before end-Feb 2027.
resolution_rule_fixed: YES if El Niño conditions (NOAA CPC) persist through February 2027; NO if ENSO returns to neutral/La Niña before end-Feb 2027.
notes: Stated as WMO near 100%; capped at 0.90 (no 1.0). NOAA Oct 2026: strong-to-very-strong through JFM 2027 (>83%).
